question: What do we know about GTM strategies that work well for developer tools and SaaS platforms?

relevant_patterns.statement: Developer-first GTM (community, open source, documentation) shows 3-4x better CAC efficiency than direct enterprise sales for infrastructure and SaaS tools
relevant_patterns.action_implication: For developer-facing ventures, prioritize community building and documentation in first 3 months. Budget 15-20% of early marketing spend to developer community and examples.

relevant_patterns.statement: B2B SaaS ventures with CAC/LTV ratio <0.2 show 2-3x faster growth trajectory than those with ratio >0.5
relevant_patterns.action_implication: Validate unit economics by week 8 post-launch. Low CAC/LTV ratios (<0.2) indicate GTM-product fit and should trigger aggressive scaling; high ratios (>0.5) require GTM overhaul.

relevant_patterns.statement: Freemium model with self-serve onboarding drives 40% faster time-to-first-value than trial-based model for B2B SaaS platforms
relevant_patterns.action_implication: For developer-targeting SaaS, implement freemium model with immediate hands-on access. Avoid lengthy trial signup flows.

synthesis: Memory shows that developer-first GTM (community, open source, documentation) is 3-4x more efficient than enterprise sales for developer tools. Combined with freemium self-serve models and strong unit economics (CAC/LTV <0.2), this approach drives 2-3x faster growth. Early focus on developer community in first 3 months is critical.
